quick_notes.title: Aptitude Recap
quick_notes.detail: Vol Sphere (4/3 pir3). Vol Cone (1/3 pir2h). HCF*LCM: Prod. Mode: 3Med-2Mean. 360 deg: 100%.
quick_notes.explanation: The volume of a sphere, which is the amount of space inside a perfectly round ball, is calculated using the formula four-thirds times pi times the radius cubed, written as 4/3 pi r cubed. The volume of a cone, which is a three-dimensional shape with a circular base that narrows to a point, is one-third times pi times the radius squared times the height, written as 1/3 pi r squared h. For any two numbers, the product of their Highest Common Factor (HCF), the largest number that divides both exactly, and their Lowest Common Multiple (LCM), the smallest number that both divide into exactly, equals the product of the two original numbers. In statistics, the mode, which is the most frequent value in a set, can be found using the formula 3 times the median (the middle value when the numbers are sorted) minus 2 times the mean (the average of all values). A full circle has 360 degrees, and this represents 100 percent of the circle, so each 1 percent of the circle equals 3.6 degrees.

quick_notes.title: Physics Recap
quick_notes.detail: Newton 3rd (Rocket). Concave (Myopia). Light Year (Distance). SI Temp (Kelvin).
quick_notes.explanation: Newton's third law of motion states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction; a rocket works by expelling gas downward, which pushes the rocket upward. A concave lens is a lens that curves inward, and it is used to correct myopia, which is nearsightedness, a condition where distant objects appear blurry. A light year is a unit of distance, not time, and it represents how far light travels in one year. The SI unit of temperature, meaning the International System of Units standard for measuring temperature, is the Kelvin.

quick_notes.title: Chemistry Recap
quick_notes.detail: pH Blood (7.4). Baking (NaHCO3). Washing (Na2CO3). Modern Periodic (Atomic No).
quick_notes.explanation: Here is a clear, complete mini-lesson on these chemistry points. The pH scale measures how acidic or basic a liquid is, with a value of 7 being neutral. Your blood has a pH of 7.4, which means it is slightly basic, and this is the normal level your body needs to stay healthy. Baking soda, which has the chemical formula NaHCO3, is a base used in cooking to make dough rise. Washing soda, with the formula Na2CO3, is a stronger base used for cleaning clothes. The modern periodic table arranges all known elements by their atomic number, which is the number of protons found in the nucleus of a single atom of that element.

quick_notes.title: Biology Recap
quick_notes.detail: Mitochondria (Powerhouse). Vit K (Clotting). Vit A (Eyes). Bacteria (TB). Mendel (Genetics).
quick_notes.explanation: Mitochondria are tiny structures inside your cells that act like a power plant, breaking down food to release energy for the body to use, which is why they are called the powerhouse of the cell. Vitamin K is a nutrient that helps your blood form clots to stop bleeding when you get a cut. Vitamin A is a nutrient that keeps your eyes healthy and helps you see in dim light. Tuberculosis, often shortened to TB, is a serious disease caused by a type of germ called bacteria that usually attacks the lungs. Gregor Mendel was a scientist who discovered the basic rules of how traits, like eye color, are passed from parents to children, and his work is the foundation of the science of genetics.

quick_notes.title: Science in TN
quick_notes.detail: Focus on Samacheer book facts. Practical applications in TN industry/health.
quick_notes.explanation: Science in Tamil Nadu (TN) means the study of natural things like physics, chemistry, and biology, and the knowledge from the Samacheer Kalvi textbooks, which are the state's standard school books. A key fact from these books is that the Tamil Nadu government has a special program called the Tamil Nadu Science and Technology Centre (TNSTC), which runs science museums and planetariums in cities like Chennai and Coimbatore to help students see science in action. For practical applications in industry, TN is famous for its automobile factories in places like Chennai and Hosur, where companies use chemistry to make car parts and physics to build engines, and for its textile mills in Coimbatore that use science to dye and weave cotton. In health, TN uses science in its many government hospitals and medical colleges, like the ones in Chennai and Madurai, where doctors apply biology and chemistry to treat diseases and perform surgeries, and the state also runs the Tamil Nadu Health System Project (TNHSP) to improve healthcare for everyone using modern medical tools.
